What do you think of NoSql like MongoDB?

Favorite sql DB?

I have worked with Oracle RDBMS and MS SQL Server. Every organization I've worked for has used SQL Server, and it's my preference. I haven't worked with Oracle since 10g. It was pretty close to T-SQL though in terms of syntax once they made join syntax follow ANSI standards.

I haven't worked with NoSQL. I think there are certain situations where NoSQL is the right choice, but it's not always the right solution. Depends a lot on requirements and development environments. It is not meant to be a whole replacement for SQL. If your needs go beyond just simply storage of data and accessing that data quickly, you're going to need SQL because of the extra functionality it offers.

For example, my organization is dealing with highly structured data where compliance (HIPAA compliance being the biggest factor) is critical. Our data models for both our various relational databases and our data warehouse are set in stone before we're loading data because we know exactly what data we're going to be loading. Data consistency is just as important for us as performance and scalability. We deal with performance issues from a non-hardware perspective by identifying our worst performing database objects and then optimizing (this is actually a big part of my job). NoSQL isn't the greatest for analytics either, and that's a huge part of our business both in terms of an OLTP structure and an OLAP structure with a BI tool sitting on top of the OLAP data warehouse. We do a lot of machine learning and regression testing using the data from our databases as well.
